title: ART-DIAL: Art Therapy as an Innovative Approach to Stress Reduction During Hemodialysis
summary: The ART-DIAL study investigates whether art therapy sessions during hemodialysis treatment can improve quality of life and psychological well-being in dialysis patients. Participating patients receive weekly art therapy sessions at their dialysis bedside over a 12-week period. The study combines questionnaires on quality of life, stress, and anxiety with personal interviews to capture both measurable and subjective changes. The goal is to establish a low-threshold, non-pharmacological therapy that transforms the often burdensome dialysis time into meaningful and therapeutically valuable time.

interventions.name: Participating patients receive weekly 45-60 minute art therapy sessions at their dialysis bedside over a 12-week period.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Chronic hemodialysis requirement for at least 3 months
Regular hemodialysis treatment (at least 2×/week) at Robert Bosch Hospital Stuttgart
Sufficient German language skills to participate in interviews and complete questionnaires
Written informed consent after comprehensive patient information
Exclusion criteria:
Severe cognitive impairment that makes study participation impossible
Severe visual impairment that makes performing visual artistic activities impossible
Acute severe psychiatric disorders (active psychosis, severe mania)
Lack of capacity to consent
Expected kidney transplantation or change of dialysis center within the next 3 months
Participation in another interventional study with psychological well-being or quality of life as primary endpoint
